description: Gmail connection is started, confirmed and disconnected by the business owner only, and a Gmail OAuth callback links nothing until the user who started it confirms it (COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 items 4 and 5; R0-07 review ST-2 and ST-3). GET /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/auth-url, the new POST /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/confirm and DELETE /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail carry AuthGuard + BusinessGuard and GmailService.assertConnectAuthority: the OWNER membership or Business.ownerId (the rule IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner applies) and SUPER_ADMIN (the BusinessGuard platform bypass); every other member gets 403 {code:'GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY'}. The signed OAuth state (HMAC-SHA256 with GOOGLE_STATE_SECRET, single use per process as R0-07 made it) now carries the initiating user id, the business id, a nonce and a 10-minute expiry. GET /commerce/gmail/callback stays public (Google redirects the browser; the web proxy forwards no session) and links nothing: a verified state that names a user has its code exchanged and the tokens stored as a PENDING connector_accounts row (provider GOOGLE, service GMAIL, tokens encrypted with encryptToken, settings {purpose, userId, nonce, pendingExpiresAt} with a 15-minute window; existing table, no schema change), then redirects gmail=pending&pending=<id>. Only that user, still the owner (or SUPER_ADMIN), confirming that id on that business within the window, once, activates it (Business.gmail*); anything else answers 404 {code:'GMAIL_PENDING_NOT_FOUND'} and links nothing. An expired, replayed, forged or user-less state redirects gmail=error&reason=invalid_state with no token exchange. Google's token exchange and userinfo are stubbed in process (no network). Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/gmail-connect-binding.integration.test.ts src/modules/commerce/gmail.service.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-cmf5-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/gmail-connect-binding.json --report .proof/r0-cmf5-vitest.json. Every case of the two files is required and no other case is admitted (allowAdditionalCases false: the two it.todo follow-ups are now real cases, D-I and the web suite); requireReportSuccess keeps every reported case binding. RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-CMF4-SEND-EMAIL-ORDER-repair (acfda3e6; tests-first commit c788e635): the integration suite failed 19 of 25 (STAFF auth-url 200 with a Google URL; ADMIN and STAFF revenue:admin 200; the state named no user; the distinguished owner 403 from ModuleScopeGuard; the owner's state completed in a stranger's request redirected gmail=success and linked the stranger's mailbox; a signed user-less state linked; no confirm route; STAFF revenue:write DELETE gmail 200 and cleared the mailbox; B05 and B12 failed there only because their first step expects gmail=pending) and the spec failed 9 of 9. Passing on the base (negative controls): X01, A06 (non-member 403, anonymous 401), B06 (expired state), B07 (forged or edited state), C02 (owner disconnect), X02 (no outbound beyond the Google stub). REVIEW REPAIRS (pkt/R0-CMF5-GMAIL-CONNECT-BINDING-repair; R0-CMF5 review ST-CMF5-1..5, CR-CMF5-1..5): GET /commerce/businesses/:b/gmail/pending/:id (OWNER only, bound to the user the state names, returns the staged mailbox and no token) and POST .../gmail/confirm now requires {pendingId, email}, email equal (case-insensitively) to the staged mailbox, else 409 GMAIL_PENDING_EMAIL_MISMATCH and the row stays (D01-D03, U11); both callbacks refuse a request whose ambient tenant (TenantInterceptor) is not the state's business, before any token exchange, proved with TenantInterceptor as APP_INTERCEPTOR and the Prisma tenant context provider installed for the whole suite (E01-E02, H03, U10); confirm (connect/replace) and every disconnect write one team_activity_logs row naming the actor in the change's transaction (F01, I02, U12); PENDING rows past their window are swept on stage, preview, confirm and status, and a disconnect removes every PENDING Gmail row of the business (G01-G03, U13-U14); POST /connect/google-suite/businesses/:b/auth-url applies the Gmail owner rule whenever gmail is requested (the default set includes it), its state names the caller, and its callback stages a Gmail grant as the same PENDING connection (redirect /app/commerce?gmail=pending) instead of writing Business.gmail*; POST /connectors/businesses/:b/disconnect|reconnect/gmail go through GmailService.disconnectGmail (owner rule, pending removal, audit) before the registry (H01-H04, I01-I02). RED-BEFORE on pkt/R0-CMF5-GMAIL-CONNECT-BINDING (929fd95d) with the repaired tests: 20 of 54 failed (D01-D03, E01, F01, G01, G03, H01-H04, I01-I02, X02 and U10-U14; E02 failed there only through E01's residue and is now independent); G02 passed on the base (the base already removed rows older than the window on a new stage).
notes: Owner ruling D-11 (2026-10-31): business configuration is OWNER only. The mailbox invoices, reminders, receipts and quotes are sent from (GmailService.sendEmail) is business configuration, so connecting, replacing and disconnecting it follows D-11, as R0-08c did for plan changes. The rule is restated in GmailService.assertConnectAuthority (CommerceModule does not import IdentityModule), with the same two owner arms and the SUPER_ADMIN bypass. ModuleScopeGuard was removed from auth-url and DELETE gmail: a revenue scope admits no one the owner rule refuses, and ModuleScopeGuard refused a distinguished owner with no membership row. GET .../gmail/status and the inbox and send routes keep their revenue scopes.

PENDING storage: connector_accounts (ConnectorAccount) is an existing tenant-scoped table with no other reader or writer in apps/server; its token columns are ciphertext by contract (token-encryption-coverage HANDLED_ELSEWHERE), so the pending tokens go through core/crypto/token-crypto encryptToken and are decrypted only at confirmation, when they move to the Business.gmail* columns the Prisma token-encryption extension encrypts. Every call names businessId. A newer consent by the same user replaces that user's unconfirmed pending row, and pending rows of the business past the window are removed when a new one is staged. The pending id is gmc_ plus 24 random bytes (base64url) and reaches only the browser that completed consent.

The callback cannot be bound to a session on this base: the API authenticates by Bearer token only and the web proxy (apps/web/src/app/api/commerce/gmail/callback/route.ts) fetches the API server-to-server with no session, so binding is by the state's userId plus the authenticated confirmation. A foreign user's confirmation is refused at confirm time (403 GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY for a non-owner, 404 GMAIL_PENDING_NOT_FOUND for an owner or SUPER_ADMIN who is not the user the state names); the callback itself redirects gmail=error for expired, replayed, forged and user-less states.

Review repairs extended the write set (recorded as a deviation): core/connectors/google-suite.controller.ts, core/connectors/google-suite.service.ts and core/connectors/connector.controller.ts (ST-CMF5-1), and apps/web/src/app/app/commerce/hooks/use-commerce-integrations.ts, apps/web/src/app/app/marketing/hooks/use-marketing.ts, apps/web/src/app/app/commerce/page.tsx with apps/web/src/app/app/commerce/__tests__/gmail-connect-confirm.test.tsx (CR-CMF5-1, CR-CMF5-2: the owner's confirm step reads gmail=pending&pending=<id>, previews, asks 'Connect <email>?' and POSTs {pendingId, email}; GMAIL_OWNER_ONLY refusals are shown, never reported as success). ConnectorModule (core, global) does not import CommerceModule, so the connector routes resolve GmailService from the application container (ModuleRef, strict false) and fail closed with 503 when it is absent.
